name: Axel Voss - Proposition de résolution (ensemble du texte)
title: REPORT on copyright and generative artificial intelligence – opportunities and challenges
part_text:
The European Parliament sets out its position on copyright and generative artificial intelligence. It asks the European Commission to act: clarify how existing copyright rules apply when AI models are trained on protected works, require AI providers to be transparent about the content they use, give creators and press publishers real control over that use, and ensure they are paid fairly. It also says content produced purely by AI should not get copyright protection. This is an opinion; it does not itself change the law.

- **What changes:** Nothing yet. Parliament asks the Commission to clarify rules, require transparency and fair pay, and consider new licensing tools.
- **Who it affects:** AI providers, creators, press publishers, and the European Union Intellectual Property Office, which may manage opt-outs and licensing support.
- **What happens next:** The Commission decides whether to propose new laws or guidance; Parliament also wants a quick review of the current copyright rules.
